title: CLO2024.1 - Virtual Model Editor
description: CLO2024.1 Virtual Model Editor Upgrade — Partial measurement lines are now movable, providing a more intuitive dimension editing interface, and allowing adjustments to bust and crotch measurements. Follow CLO technical experts to learn more about new virtual model design features!
transcript:
Hello everyone!  
In version 2024.1, the virtual model editor has been optimized.  
Adjusting the size is more intuitive and accurate, and it can adjust the shape of the model’s chest and other specific parts.  
Let’s take a closer look.  

First, with the update of the virtual model editor, we added a new default virtual model, which is more suitable for the updated virtual model editor.  
In the virtual model editor window, you can see the new default model name; the model name is v2.1, and the previous model name is v1.1.  
Other virtual models can be found in the Connect store.  

Open the old version of the virtual model editor here.  
In the main menu, find the virtual model editor.  
Open the virtual model editor.  
At this point, you can see that if you use the virtual model editor to open it,  
or open one that was previously created in version 2024.1,  
the AVS file will be imported into the new virtual model editor.  
A warning window will pop up in the virtual model editor.  
This is because the size data of the new virtual model editor has changed.  
Therefore, the model’s body shape may change according to the updated size data.  
So, when creating a virtual model, you need to pay attention to this.  

Now, the updated virtual model editor is divided into two aspects: size and shape.  
In this section, you can choose to preset the size and modify the unit.  
In the previous version, all size content related to the details of the whole body was included here.  
In the previous version, you could choose between simple, basic, high-end human body, or human body models in the details.  
Each type of size project that can be entered and modified is different.  

After optimization, the UI now focuses on the basic and high-end model options.  
You can freely choose and enter the required size project.  
Click on the gear icon in the upper right corner to display the editable measurement values.  
At this time, all editable measurement values will appear at the bottom.  
You can choose the measurement values of the size you need below.  
The size selected and displayed in blue is the size that can be edited.  
Unselected projects will not be displayed during editing and cannot be adjusted directly.  
But they will automatically adjust to the appropriate size according to the input value in the existing measurement size.  

After selection,  
click the exit button in the upper right corner to complete the settings.  
You can see that only the projects we just selected are displayed and editable under size.  

In addition, in the previous version, the model size of the virtual model was adjusted based on the algorithm.  
This means that when you modify the height, shoulder height, chest, and other full-body sizes,  
it will create the appropriate body shape according to the algorithm and the data you input.  

We have added the function of individually modifying each size project.  
This function is represented by the link icon on the right side of the width and height.  
If you want to modify the virtual model in the same way as before,  
you can click on the icon and activate it to modify the virtual model size.  
You can see that the sizes below are automatically adjusted with the adjustment of the width and height values.  

On the contrary, if you click on the icon and deactivate the connection again,  
you can change the width and height values independently.  
For example, the chest and height below will remain unchanged.  
If you want to modify the model height within the same size preset, you can use this function.  

The new version can also modify the size of the cup.  
First, select the chest size in the width and enter the value,  
then enter the chest size below.  
You can see that the chest is fixed and the cup size will change.  
In this way, you can create a virtual model with different cup sizes.  

The following shapes include the adjustment of the arm length,  
adjustment of the head circumference, and the new width adjustment.  
For men, you can also adjust the volume of the waist.  
In the previous version, the waist of the model was not adjustable.  
This may cause simulation problems when creating tight clothing, such as swimsuits and underwear.  
Now you can freely adjust the waist of the model,  
making it more convenient to create swimsuits, underwear, and other clothes.  

Next, you can see the virtual model in the 3D window on the left side.  
Previously, the measurement line position on the virtual model was fixed and could not be modified.  
In the new version, we added the function to move the measurement line on the virtual model.  
You can drag and move the measurement line position directly to adjust the size of the virtual model.  

First of all, when you open the virtual model editor window,  
the default will automatically start the virtual model measurement tool.  
Use this tool to drag the actual line on the model to measure.  
You can see that the selected measurement line is displayed in yellow.  
There will be virtual arrows at the top and bottom of the moving middle line.  
These arrows indicate the maximum range within which the measurement line can be moved.  

To avoid exceeding the range of the selected measurement line,  
you can move the measurement line to the desired position  
without overlapping with other measurement lines.  
The range of movement for the measurement line is limited to three centimeters above and below.  

After moving the measurement line to the desired position,  
modify the corresponding size in the virtual model editor window on the right side.  
You can check the effect of the modification in the 3D window.  

If you want to restore the original position,  
you can right-click on the measurement line to reset the position or reset all positions.  

This is the update and improvement content of the virtual model editor function in version 2024.1.  
I hope that you can create a virtual model that satisfies you more easily and accurately by using these functions.

chunks.content: ## Overview of the Virtual Model Editor Update in CLO 2024.1 This section introduces the key improvements in the virtual model editor in CLO version 2024.1, highlighting enhanced size adjustment accuracy and new capabilities for modifying specific body parts such as the chest. --- ## New Default Virtual Model and Compatibility The update introduces a new default virtual model named **v2.1**, designed specifically to work with the updated virtual model editor. The previous default model was **v1.1**. Additional virtual models remain available through the Connect store. When opening older AVS files created in previous versions, the new editor imports the data but displays a warning. This is because size data formats have changed, potentially altering the model’s body shape. Users should be cautious when creating or modifying models from older files to account for these changes. --- ## Size and Shape Adjustments: Interface and Functionality The updated virtual model editor separates adjustments into two main aspects: **size** and **shape**. ### Size Presets and Editable Measurements - Users can now choose between **basic** and **high-end** human body size presets. - Clicking the gear icon in the upper right reveals editable measurement values related to the chosen size preset. - Only selected measurement projects appear and are editable; unselected ones adjust automatically based on input values. - After selecting measurements, clicking the exit button confirms the settings and limits editing to those specific projects. ### Individual vs. Linked Size Adjustments - Previously, resizing was algorithm-driven: modifying height or chest automatically adjusted related body proportions. - In 2024.1, a **link icon** appears beside width and height values, representing whether size parameters are linked. - **Linked mode (activated link icon):** Adjusting width or height triggers automatic proportional changes across related measurements. - **Unlinked mode (deactivated link icon):** Width and height can be adjusted independently without affecting other measurements, allowing more precise control over specific dimensions. ### Cup Size and Chest Adjustments - Users can modify **cup size** independently from chest width. - Adjust chest width first, then input the chest size below it. - This allows creation of virtual models with varying cup sizes while maintaining chest width. --- ## New Shape Adjustments and Previously Unavailable Controls ### New Adjustable Parameters - **Arm length** - **Head circumference** - **Model width** - **Waist volume** (newly added for men) ### Importance of Waist Adjustment - Waist adjustment was not available in previous versions. - This led to difficulties simulating tight clothing such as swimsuits and underwear. - Now, the waist can be freely adjusted, improving garment fitting accuracy for tight apparel. --- ## Interactive 3D Measurement Line Editing ### Measurement Line Movement - The 3D window displays the virtual model with measurement lines. - Previously, measurement line positions were fixed. - The update enables users to **drag and move measurement lines** directly on the model. ### Using the Measurement Tool - The editor automatically activates the virtual model measurement tool on opening. - Selected measurement lines highlight in yellow.

chunks.content: - Now, the waist can be freely adjusted, improving garment fitting accuracy for tight apparel. --- ## Interactive 3D Measurement Line Editing ### Measurement Line Movement - The 3D window displays the virtual model with measurement lines. - Previously, measurement line positions were fixed. - The update enables users to **drag and move measurement lines** directly on the model. ### Using the Measurement Tool - The editor automatically activates the virtual model measurement tool on opening. - Selected measurement lines highlight in yellow. - Virtual arrows at the ends indicate the maximum allowed movement range (±3 cm). - Measurement lines cannot overlap or exceed this range, ensuring logical adjustments. ### Applying Changes - After positioning a measurement line, users modify the corresponding size value in the editor window. - Changes are reflected immediately in the 3D model view. - Right-clicking a measurement line resets it to the original or resets all lines simultaneously. --- ## Summary of Improvements in CLO 2024.1 Virtual Model Editor The 2024.1 update enhances the virtual model editor by introducing: - A new default model optimized for the editor. - Clear separation of size presets with selectable and editable measurements. - Optional linking/unlinking of size parameters for flexible adjustments. - Independent cup size modification. - New shape controls including waist volume adjustment for men. - Interactive 3D measurement line repositioning with controlled movement range. These improvements enable more intuitive, precise, and versatile virtual model creation suited for detailed garment simulation such as swimsuits and underwear.
